implementation_notes: pika is the standard Python AMQP client and it is callback-first: basic_consume(queue, on_message_callback=cb, auto_ack=False) binds a callback with signature (channel, method, properties, body) and start_consuming() blocks the calling thread while the library dispatches each delivery to it; the callback replaces the classic endpoint object, and auto_ack defaults to False so acknowledgement is explicit. At transport level the stdlib analogue is the asyncio Protocol callback, where the transport calls protocol.data_received() - the same inversion, and writing it by hand means building the container a broker library would otherwise provide.
pitfalls: auto_ack=True (or acking before the work is durable) loses messages if the process dies inside the callback.

pika's BlockingConnection is not thread-safe and dispatches callbacks on the calling thread: a blocking callback stalls consumption - offload work or use an async client such as aio-pika for concurrency.
basic_nack(requeue=True) on a poisoned message loops forever; requeue=False and dead-letter instead.
start_consuming() blocks until the consumer is cancelled; forgetting to cancel on shutdown leaves the process hanging.
